title: Rust FFI Boundaries
summary: Learn what crosses a C-style boundary: repr(C) layout, extern "C" functions, callbacks, raw pointers, owned handles, error codes and buffers.
description: Rust talks to C through a narrow contract: fixed struct layouts, plain functions, raw pointers and integer error codes. This track teaches that contract without needing a C compiler. Both sides of every boundary are written in Rust, so you practise the rules a real binding must follow: controlling field order and padding, passing extern "C" functions as pointers, threading a context pointer through callbacks, moving ownership with Box::into_raw and Box::from_raw, keeping panics from crossing the line, and filling caller-supplied buffers snprintf-style. A capstone builds a small C-ABI key-value library. The runner cannot link real C code into a Rust program, so no lesson proves compatibility with a C compiler; see docs/language-interop-feasibility.md.
outcomes: Design and implement a C-style API in Rust with explicit layout, ownership and error conventions.
